headline.title: Jackie is alive and stable, in expert hands.
headline.lede: Big Bear's beloved bald eagle was rescued on the night of Friday, July 17 after an altercation with two younger eagles left her grounded by the lake. She is now at the Ojai Raptor Center — alert, perching, and eating with assistance while veterinarians await her full diagnostic results. Shadow is home, watching over the territory and still feeding Sandy and Luna.

statuses.state: Stable · in care at Ojai Raptor Center
Fledged in June, being fed by Shadow

updates.title: Community response tops 8,400 donations
updates.body: The Ojai Raptor Center has received tens of thousands of dollars from Jackie's worldwide family — more than 8,400 individual donations to their Bald Eagle Rehabilitation Campaign as of Monday. The center reminds everyone that updates will come through their email list and social media, and asks that the hotline stay clear for animal emergencies.

updates.title: Underweight but alert, perching, and eating
updates.body: The Ojai Raptor Center reports Jackie is alert, perching, and eating with assistance. Her physical exam found no fractures and no major wounds — she arrived lethargic and underweight, which is why full diagnostic testing matters. Results are expected within days.

updates.title: It's officially Jackie — and she's in specialist hands
updates.body: What early reports could only call an eagle 'believed to be Jackie' has been confirmed by Friends of Big Bear Valley: the rescued eagle is Jackie. She has been transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center, a facility specializing in birds of prey, for advanced care and a comprehensive medical evaluation.

updates.title: Shadow holds the territory — six fish delivered
updates.body: While Jackie recovers, Shadow is doing what he has always done: guarding the territory and providing. Friends of Big Bear Valley counted six fish deliveries for Sandy and Luna, who fledged in late June and are flying well.

updates.title: Rescued in the small hours by 'Jackie's angels'
updates.body: After being found grounded on the shoreline at Dana Point Park on Friday evening — apparently after defending her territory against two subadult eagles — Jackie was watched over for hours by residents, visitors, and the Fawnskin fire crew under Captain Dennis Jones. The San Dimas Raptor Rescue Team of the LA County Parks Department completed the rescue around 2:00 a.m. Saturday.

unknowns: Her full diagnostic results — bloodwork and lab tests were still pending at the last official update, expected within days.
Why she was underweight — whether the fight caused her condition, or her condition preceded the fight.
How long rehabilitation will take, and when (or whether) a release date might be set. No official timeline exists yet.
Whether the two subadult eagles will linger in the territory.

rumors.body: As of the most recent official updates (July 20–21), Jackie is stable, alert, perching, and eating. Any claim otherwise did not come from FOBBV or the Ojai Raptor Center.

rumors.claim: She was badly wounded in the attack.
rumors.body: Her physical exam found no fractures and no major wounds. The concern is that she was underweight and lethargic — which is why diagnostics matter more than the fight itself.

rumors.claim: Sandy and Luna have been abandoned.
rumors.body: Sandy and Luna fledged successfully in late June and are flying. Shadow is actively hunting for them and guarding the territory — six fish deliveries were observed in a single stretch.

rumors.claim: It might not even be Jackie.
rumors.body: This was a fair question in the first days — early reports said 'believed to be Jackie.' FOBBV has since confirmed her identity.

rumors.claim: She'll be released on [any specific date].
rumors.body: No release timeline has been announced by anyone official. Rehabilitation decisions will follow her diagnostics and recovery — expect this to be measured in weeks, not days, and let the professionals set the pace.

rumors.claim: Calling the raptor center shows support.
rumors.body: The Ojai Raptor Center has specifically asked people not to call or text their hotline — those lines are for animals in urgent need. Updates will come through their email list and social media.

events.title: The first clutch
events.body: Jackie lays two eggs as the new season opens.

events.title: Ravens strike
events.body: Both eggs are breached by a pair of ravens — a heartbreak this nest has known before.

events.title: A second chance
events.body: Jackie lays a second clutch of two eggs. The watch begins again.

events.title: Two hatches
events.body: Chick one arrives at 9:33 p.m. on April 4; chick two follows the next morning at 8:30 a.m.

events.title: Sandy & Luna
events.body: Bear Valley third-graders choose the winning names from some 63,000 entries.

events.title: Fledge days
events.body: Sandy leaves the nest first (an 'accidental flight'); Luna follows the next morning, landing in a tree beside Shadow.

events.title: Jackie is found grounded
events.body: After an altercation with two subadult eagles — apparently over territory and food — Jackie is found on the shoreline at Dana Point Park, on the lake's northwest side, unable to fly. Residents and visitors stay beside her and go for help.

events.title: The fire crew stands watch
events.body: Captain Dennis Jones and the Fawnskin fire crew guard her for hours, keeping wildlife and onlookers away. FOBBV would later call everyone involved 'Jackie's angels.'

events.title: Rescue complete
events.body: The San Dimas Raptor Rescue Team of the LA County Parks Department arrives in the small hours and safely secures her.

events.title: To Ojai, and confirmation
events.body: Jackie is transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for specialized care. Her identity is confirmed: it is Jackie.

events.title: Stable, alert, eating
events.body: No fractures, no major wounds. Underweight but perching and eating with assistance. Full diagnostic results expected within days.

events.title: The waiting
events.body: Shadow keeps the territory and feeds Sandy and Luna. The rest of us wait together — and let the experts work.
